In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FCM algorithm can be used to estimate the centers of a mixture of univariate normal distributions, but not of any other mixture of symmetric distributions.

, while the FCM cluster centroids are not in general consistent estimators for the centers of a mixture of symmetric distributions, they are consistent estimators for a mixture of asymmetric distributions, provided the number of data points is sufficiently large.

the fuzzy cmeans approach is useful for mixture parameter estimation in cases where the mixture subpopulations have non-overlapping component distributions, and the FCM cluster centroids are consistent estimators of mixture component centers (means) under such conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FCM approach may be useful in some cases for estimating mixture subpopulation centers, but that it cannot generally be considered as a statistically consistent approach to this problem.

FCM is a very good clustering algorithm, but it cannot be used to estimate mixture subpopulation centers in a statistically consistent manner, unless the component distributions are symmetric and the mixture has only two components.
the fuzzy cmeans clustering algorithm can be used as a useful tool for exploratory data analysis, but not as a statistical estimation procedure for mixture models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FCM algorithm should not be used as an alternative to maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) for the parameters of statistical mixtures.
, in order to use FCM for statistical mixture modeling, one must first determine the appropriate number of clusters (components).
the FCM clustering scheme should be used cautiously when the objective is to estimate the parameters of a mixture of distributions.
